---
title: "Architecture"
---

## Product direction

Cellerator is an extensible machine-learning framework whose computational
abstractions are developed around the structure of the cell and the systems it
comprises. Its governing architectural question is:

> What would machine learning look like if its computational abstractions were
> developed around the structure of the cell and the systems it comprises,
> rather than cellular systems being translated into abstractions originally
> developed for language?

The aim is to make learning cellular representations, relationships, and
dynamics as natural as learning sequences is in language-model frameworks,
without compromising general neural-network expressiveness and while exploiting
biological structure for computational efficiency. PyTorch provides tensors and
differentiable operations; sequence-model libraries provide convenient sequence
architectures. Cellerator should make cellular systems equally natural
computational subjects through a richer vocabulary for constructing models of
cells and their behavior, without imposing a particular mathematical cell object.

This original biological ML ambition governs subsequent design choices and
ecosystem analogies. Representation, architecture, learning objectives, and
execution should develop together. Stable molecular identities, conditional
interactions, overlapping regulatory modules, history, and shared learned rules
can motivate both neural abstractions and specialized layouts or kernels.
Compiler, scheduler, and distribution machinery serve those models; they do not
replace the biological modeling purpose. Building, training, and sharing cell
models describes the experience this architecture should make possible.

Biological structure adds a vocabulary and computational opportunities without
restricting general neural-network expressiveness. Dense networks, ordinary
attention, transformers, recurrent models, mixtures of experts, sparse
conditional models, dynamical systems, and arbitrary combinations remain valid.
This is an ambition for practical modeling expressiveness, not a claim of a
larger universal-approximation class. A model should gain useful choices from
biological structure rather than be required to follow a biological metaphor.

Dynamics remains a central motivation alongside learning representations and
relationships. Optional state-transition APIs preserve freedom to learn behavior
through event histories, recurrent memory, latent dynamics, and other forms;
they do not demote dynamics or privilege static encoders. No single formulation
defines every permissible biological learning problem.

PyTorch is an optional and useful integration route for learned modules,
autograd, and ordinary tensor computation. Cellerator also owns native numerical
operations, specialized CPU/GPU execution, and representations that may be dense,
sparse, ragged, event based, relational, externally owned, custom, or hybrid.
An optional framework adapter is an implementation boundary; it does not make
learning secondary to a simulation runtime. Cellerator provides reusable machinery;
Karyoplast, Cytoplast, Blastback, and future consumers own application-specific
biological assumptions and scientific validation.

The library is early and not near complete. The target architecture is a
direction for organizing new work and moving complete units, not a claim that
all target packages or APIs exist.

For the user facing modeling vocabulary and the new Python packages, see the
[biological modeling framework](biological_framework.qmd). Its APIs are in
rapid development; package presence does not imply scientific validation or
accelerated backend support.

## Organizing the learning problem

The architecture serves three connected ambitions: **expressiveness** in
describing models, **learning** suited to biological questions, and **efficiency**
from structure a model contains or discovers. Design a capability across these
concerns rather than beginning with a required cell lifecycle or sparse format.

| Concern | Architectural responsibility |
|---|---|
| Representations and observations | Express what is measured, what the model represents, and how they relate, without treating a transcriptional profile, embedding, or latent state as a complete cell by definition. |
| Neural composition and relationships | Compose ordinary neural operators with learned or supplied biological relationships, contextual interactions, overlapping modules, and optional memory. Allow relationships beyond those already known. |
| Objectives and training | Express the biological question through conditioning, supervision, observation models, losses, and training procedures. Distinguish what the objective constrains from what a representation is hoped to contain. |
| Optional dynamics and coupling | Provide state transitions, continuous evolution, stochastic events, histories, and interacting populations when a model needs them. These are composable capabilities rather than a mandatory model form. |
| Numerical and physical execution | Implement the chosen mathematical computation with appropriate derivatives, layouts, precision, reuse, scheduling, and resource ownership. Exploit structure without silently changing model semantics. |

These are responsibilities, not a required sequence of runtime stages or a new
mandatory object hierarchy. A static representation learner can use biological
attention without a transition rule; a perturbation model can predict responses
without simulating every intermediate state; a recurrent model can maintain
persistent cellular state. Each is a first-class use case.

Attention already expresses learned, context-dependent interactions. The
architectural question is which participants, representations, conditioning,
and objectives best express the biological problem. A sequence encoding or
masked reconstruction objective is one choice, not the default definition of
cellular learning. Reconstruction of observations alone does not establish that
the responsible dynamics or intervention responses have been learned.

`Cell`, `Model`, step contexts, events, and trajectory APIs support the models
for which their contracts are useful. They do not define every permissible
network or require every learning problem to be expressed as explicit cellular
state transitions. Conventional neural modules and alternative representations
must remain composable without adopting those APIs.

## Modeling and neural-network backbone

**Conceptual direction recorded 2026-10-31.** The missing backbone is the coherent
modeling experience that connects biological information, learned computation,
and the questions a model is trained to answer. Existing numerical, interaction,
state, and execution mechanisms are foundations for it. Their presence does not
by itself provide a complete biological neural-network framework.

The following six concerns are complementary responsibilities, not a mandatory
pipeline, package layout, class hierarchy, or implementation plan. They preserve
the biological ML ambition above while keeping the public experience minimal.

### Biological information and learned representations

Distinguish molecular identity, measured values, experimental context, history,
and inferred information. Feature identity should survive storage reordering;
repeated events involving one gene remain distinct occurrences. Models may use
expression features, event histories, molecular graphs, latent arrays, regulatory
memory, or hybrids. A cell makes the cellular subject and relevant information
addressable without asserting a complete or uniquely defined biological state.
Compatibility between representations depends on their meaning and available
information, not merely matching dimensions.

### General trainable composition

Provide coherent composition of learned modules, shared parameters, gradients,
and ordinary neural operations with structured biological computations. Dense
transformations, normalization, residual connections, attention, recurrence,
and conditional modules should remain natural choices. Reuse established neural
infrastructure where it serves these needs; the ambition does not require
reimplementing every conventional layer or optimizer. Cellerator's contribution
is preserving useful biological identities and relationships through composition
without repeatedly reconstructing them in application-specific glue. Native
execution and alternative backends remain possible.

### Learned interactions

Make it natural to express which participants interact, under what context,
through what learned computation, and how their contributions combine.
Participants may be genes, peaks, proteins, latent features, overlapping modules,
or cells. Relationships may be supplied, discovered, dense, sparse, or conditional;
attention belongs naturally in this family. Models should be able to learn
participation as well as interaction strengths without assigning every module a
predetermined biological role. Known regulatory structure may inform a model
without delimiting the relationships it can discover.

### History, memory, and conditional behavior

Histories, interventions, environmental conditioning, recurrent memory, and
temporal prediction should be natural architectural ingredients. Autoregressive
event models, recurrent networks, and explicit dynamical systems express
different forms of this capability. Shared parameters, cell-specific computational
context, and biological observations remain distinct. A model may learn behavior
through distributed history-dependent computation without declaring one explicit
biological state vector. Static models need neither a clock nor a transition rule.

### Readouts and learning questions

Connect representations to conditioning information, requested predictions,
available observations, targets, and objectives. Masked reconstruction, event
prediction, perturbation response, trajectory learning, and multimodal prediction
provide different constraints; preserve those differences instead of imposing a
universal loss or observation model. A shared auxiliary model can derive ATAC
predictions from suitable Karyoplast representations or context and be trained
separately or jointly, as the experiment requires. Preserve the distinction
between a measured view and a predicted one. Neither representation structure
nor an objective's name establishes the resulting scientific claim.

### Reusable model construction and training

Make these components fit together into complete trainable models, including
selected trainable or frozen components, combined objectives, heterogeneous
batches, and reusable pretrained components. Cellular encoders, conditional
predictors, event models, recurrent models, and interacting-population models
are useful conceptual families and compositions, not a fixed model catalog.
The framework should support individual and collective learning questions;
cell-level addressability does not require statistical independence or a
separate loss for every cell. Model definitions should retain their meaning
across efficient execution and reuse.

### Existing foundations and remaining capability gaps

This is the source-oriented architectural assessment recorded before the
2026-10-31 NN foundation implementation, not a
completion checklist or a replacement for the dated
[implementation record](current_implementation.qmd). The existing mechanisms
have different backend and validation boundaries. The remaining work includes
coherence and generalization of interfaces, not just adding more kernels or
renaming existing classes.

The first implementation now provides a general `Cell`, explicit dynamical
wrappers, feature encoding, relation attention, shared readouts, and a trainable
grouped-linear adapter. Read the [NN foundation guide](nn_foundation.qmd) and
[dated implementation record](current_implementation.qmd) for current contracts
and qualification. The table below preserves the motivation for that work;
the broader modeling capabilities remain open-ended.

The subsequent biological-meaning pass adds optional model-local feature
bindings, prepared occurrence relations, identity-labelled prediction queries,
explicit supervision alignment/reduction, and biological manifests beside
weights. Shared interaction programs compose existing attention with contextual
learned queries. These connect neural operations to declared participants and
learning questions while retaining raw tensor composition. Numerical conditioning
must actually alter the registered computation; descriptive context alone does
not do so. None of these interfaces supplies a universal ontology, complete
cellular state, automatic hard-topology discovery, or scientific identifiability.
Their current implementation is Python-facing; the first-class native modeling
target below remains broader.

| Concern | Existing machinery to build on | Remaining conceptual capability |
|---|---|---|
| Information and representations | Feature identities, ranked/event vocabularies, sparse and ragged state, event histories, and explicit AnnData exchange. | A coherent model-facing vocabulary spanning measured, historical, and learned information without requiring one persistent state representation. |
| Trainable composition | A small `nn` surface for Product2, mechanisms, and shared-support relations; optional Torch learned dynamics, gated interactors, event heads, and expert banks. | Natural general neural composition across structured biological representations and ordinary modules, with clear parameter and gradient ownership. |
| Interactions | Directed, bipartite, and hyperedge computations, activity gates, sparse support, worklists, and numerical attention/dispatch operations. | A unified modeling experience for learned participation, contextual computation, and aggregation across dense, sparse, and overlapping relationships. |
| History and behavior | Explicit model/cell transition APIs, external state references, trajectories, events, and population context/lifecycle mechanisms. | General history-conditioned and recurrent modeling that composes with static encoders and does not make `advance()` the universal model operation. |
| Readouts and questions | Observation callbacks, an event prediction head, observation-conditioned inference, and trajectory loss contexts. | Shared trainable auxiliary views and composable biological objectives with explicit conditioning, target, and representation dependencies. |
| Model construction and training | A trajectory-window training adapter, shared-parameter expert execution, and focused differentiable dispatch paths. | A coherent construction and training experience across static, generative, recurrent, multimodal, and population models; complete-model validation remains separate. |

Useful source entry points are the [neural interface](../python/cellerator/nn.py),
[learned adapters](../python/cellerator/adapters/torch.py),
[trajectory training adapter](../python/cellerator/adapters/training.py),
[interaction mechanisms](../python/cellerator/interactions/core.py), and
[current model/cell contracts](../python/cellerator/modeling/core.py). Read their
actual contracts before operationalizing this direction; a named module or
working primitive does not establish the broader capability in the final column.

### How the concerns combine

| Modeling case | Combination of concerns |
|---|---|
| Geneformer-like encoder | Biological feature representations, contextual interactions, aggregation, and reconstruction or representation objectives. |
| Karyoplast | Event representations, history-dependent computation, shared conditional modules, generative objectives, and auxiliary readouts. |
| Cytoplast | Many private cellular contexts using shared learned computation, with coupling, environmental inputs, and individual or collective objectives. |

These are motivating design cases, not instructions to implement those projects
inside Cellerator. Execution should exploit identities, conditional participation,
reuse, and interaction locality through suitable layouts, kernels, batching, and
placement while preserving mathematical meaning. Model sharing preserves that
meaning for reuse. Both serve the modeling and learning backbone.

Operationalization remains a separate user-directed step. This section does
not select APIs, prescribe an implementation sequence, or authorize development.
The architectural test is whether a researcher can express a biological learning
question more directly and turn it into a trainable, efficient model because
Cellerator supplies the appropriate computational vocabulary.

## First-class C++ and Python modeling {#cpp-and-python-modeling}

**Design direction recorded 2026-10-31.** Cellerator should be an intuitive
biological ML modeling framework in C++ as well as Python. Its C++ interface
should be at least as expressive for the framework's biological and neural
abstractions, with room for native extensions beyond the Python bindings.
Authoring, composing, training, and extending a model belong in both languages.
A collection of native kernels beneath a Python-only modeling layer would not
fulfil this requirement.

The C++ API should originate as an idiomatic C++ library in which models are
authored directly. Its types and composition should follow C++ needs rather
than mirror a Python class hierarchy, constructor vocabulary, or registration
pattern. Backend reuse must not turn the public API into a cosmetic wrapper
around LibTorch's frontend. Native biological components should be usable and
extensible as ordinary C++ library facilities, with Python bindings and adapters
exposing shared mechanisms rather than determining their native design.
Python-specific model composition and extensions remain legitimate.

The shared foundation is the biological meaning of the computation: feature
identities and occurrences, eligible interactions, conditioning and history,
learned representations, readouts, supervision, and parameter sharing. Neither
language should impose an explicit cell lifecycle or a universal tensor layout.
Equivalent model definitions should preserve those meanings across interfaces,
even when their syntax and extension mechanisms differ.

### Strengths to foreground

| C++ | Python |
|---|---|
| Typed model composition, generic algorithms, and compile-time specialization where they improve usability or execution. | Interactive model exploration, runtime composition, and rapid experiments with representations and objectives. |
| Direct inheritance, callables, and templates for extending biological modules and operators without a Python dependency. | Ordinary Python and `torch.nn.Module` composition, callable readouts, and custom-operation prototyping. |
| Predictable ownership and lifetimes, reusable workspaces, borrowed storage, and specialized dynamic layouts. | Convenient integration with AnnData, scientific data tools, training utilities, notebooks, and analysis workflows. |
| Native HPC embedding, CPU parallelism, CUDA integration, and control over batching, memory, and communication when needed. | Orchestration of the same native work through coarse batched calls, with access to advanced execution controls when needed. |

These are complementary strengths, not exclusive roles. C++ should support
exploratory model construction and ordinary training; Python should support
large-scale execution and novel native extensions. Python orchestration can
invoke the same native computation, so language choice alone establishes no
performance advantage.

### Intuitive authoring with an explicit advanced path

A C++ model author should be able to compose a feature encoder, a contextual
interaction, ordinary neural layers, and selected readouts around a biological
objective without writing binding code or manually wiring every allocator,
stream, and backend registration. Safe ownership defaults and ordinary C++
composition should make the common case concise. Explicit views, preparation,
storage, and stream controls should remain available when the model needs them.
Value and reference semantics, constructors, containers, and generic interfaces
should fit ordinary C++ practice. Extension should not require imitating a
Python object's attribute machinery or registration conventions.
RAII ownership must account for asynchronous work retaining borrowed resources;
returning from a host call does not necessarily end their use.

Inheritance is useful for runtime substitution and heterogeneous collections;
templates and callables are useful for typed specialization and local
composition. Use each where it helps, rather than forcing every model through
one base class or duplicating Python's object conventions. Batch execution
should not require per-cell cross-language callbacks. Native-only consumers
should be able to build and link the selected facilities without an interpreter.

Reuse existing tensor libraries, differentiation, conventional layers,
optimizers, and communication facilities. LibTorch can supply useful machinery;
its module registration and C++ ergonomics need not define Cellerator's public
modeling experience. A more convenient Cellerator interface should preserve
backend interoperability and parameter ownership rather than hide a second
parameter copy. This direction does not require a new universal autograd engine,
operator registry, or reimplementation of standard neural layers.

### Shared contracts and the current gap

Native mathematical operations should have explicit contracts independent of a
particular binding. C++ and Python composition should agree on identity/layout
effects, precision, mutation, derivatives, ownership, and lifetime. Preserve one
logical owner for shared parameters across readouts and adapters. Keep
language-specific extension points open: not every C++ template or Python
callable needs a counterpart in the other language. Supported cross-language
model exchange must declare its limits rather than promise serialization of
arbitrary user code.

For example, a gene-aware expression encoder should be natural to define and
train in C++; a Karyoplast-style history model should permit custom native
interactions and shared auxiliary readouts; a Cytoplast-style population should
embed shared learned computation in a native HPC application. Python should
offer the corresponding biological concepts alongside its data and training
ecosystem. These remain motivating model families, not architectures imposed
by the framework.

The current NN foundation's generic cell binding, feature encoding, relation
attention, and readout composer are Python-facing. Existing C++ modeling,
tokenization, numerical, and CUDA APIs provide foundations, but do not establish
equivalent complete native model authoring and training. Closing that gap is
architectural work still to design and qualify. The first milestone's ordinary
PyTorch training route remains valid; this clarification neither relabels it as
C++ parity nor authorizes a new implementation push.

## Cells, representations, and auxiliary views

**Design request recorded 2026-10-31.** Preserve this requirement when refining
the elementary classes. It is design intent, not an implemented API contract or
authorization to resume development. Exact class boundaries and method names
remain open. The public API should be intuitive and minimal, and its eventual
implementation should support efficient native and batched execution.

A `Cell` should make a cellular subject and its associated information
addressable in a learning problem. When bound to a learned model, it can be a
lightweight handle to that model's representation or computational context for
the cell. A "pointer to a latent" is a useful intuition, but must not become a
requirement for one explicit, persistently materialized latent vector. Relevant
information may be distributed across structured features, event history,
attention context, recurrent memory, or several learned representations.
History and behavior under specified conditions remain native modeling concepts;
an instantaneous view is only one possible selection of cellular information.

### Motivating request: an auxiliary ATAC model for Karyoplast

Given suitable supporting data, a user should be able to train a separate
auxiliary model that derives another view of a Karyoplast cell, such as its
ATAC peaks. Attach the readout to the shared learned program so many cells can
use the same auxiliary parameters. A cell's individual history or context
determines its prediction without requiring its own copy of either model.
The auxiliary readout may itself be a substantial learned model; it is not
restricted to a linear head.

The readout's source must be selectable: a named representation, intermediate
features, history-dependent context, or a composition of available features.
Do not require all readouts to consume a single canonical cell embedding. A
convenient final embedding may discard information useful to an auxiliary
task. The availability of training data does not by itself establish that a
particular representation retains the information needed for the new readout.

Training only the auxiliary model with a frozen base and jointly training the
base and auxiliary model are distinct, explicit choices. Preserve the
appropriate gradient paths. Measured ATAC data and model-predicted ATAC views
must remain distinguishable; auxiliary predictions are not new measurements.
The same mechanism should accommodate other readouts and model families.

Illustrative syntax only; these methods are not established public APIs:

```python
karyoplast.add_view("atac", atac_decoder, source="regulatory_features")

cell = karyoplast.bind(history=events)
peaks = cell.predict("atac")

# The same request over a batch of cell handles.
peaks = karyoplast.predict(cells, view="atac")
```

The durable requirement is this small modeling experience, not these exact
spellings. Users should not have to construct separate task, view, and session
objects for every prediction. Those concepts may support the implementation
and advanced composition without imposing a mandatory public object hierarchy.
Auxiliary views should be usable with static encoders, autoregressive models,
recurrent systems, and explicit dynamical models alike.

### Performance and ownership requirements

- Keep shared base and auxiliary parameters separate from lightweight cell
  handles and cell-specific context. Avoid parameter duplication per cell.
- Compute requested views lazily and reuse valid intermediate representations.
  Do not require dense state decoding, permanent materialization of every
  possible view, or unnecessary host/device copies.
- Make batches a native execution path rather than a Python loop over cell
  objects. Preserve sparse, ragged, structured, and device-resident data where
  their operation contracts permit it.
- Retain gradients when training requires them; a view must not silently detach
  a representation or force a conversion through a non-differentiable format.
- Cache reuse must account for the source history/context, selected
  representation and conditioning, and base/readout parameter revisions.
  Updating a model or changing the cell's available information must not return
  a stale prediction as current.
- Distinguish semantically necessary recurrent memory from reconstructible
  caches and temporary activations. Physical eviction must preserve the
  model's declared information dependencies.

These are design constraints and performance goals, not measured speedup
claims. The 2026-10-31 implementation separates the old state/clock/`advance()`
wrapper into `DynamicalCell`, supplies a general information-bound `Cell`, and
adds `ModelWithViews` for explicitly selected shared readouts. See the
[NN foundation guide](nn_foundation.qmd). It reuses one forward result within a
call and introduces no persistent cache. Further representation, execution,
and modeling capabilities still require their own scoped development.

## Scientific questions and identifiability

Preserving identities and making context-dependent interactions explicit may
make a question clearer in the architecture and its learning objective. This
can make relevant components easier to investigate. Biological naming or
structure alone does not establish causality, molecular interpretation, or
identifiability, and known regulatory relationships need not be hardcoded.

Identifiability is relative to a question, an admissible model family,
assumptions, and the observation experiment. Appropriately sampled dynamics,
natural excitation, lineage, interventions, or other forcing can constrain a
feature within a defensible model class. Identifying a dynamical feature does
not require identifying every latent coordinate or biochemical realization.
Latent-state ambiguity therefore cannot justify a universal impossibility claim.

Cellerator should make the intended question and available constraints natural
to express in models and training. GlassHelix investigates which inferential
conclusions are formally justified under those conditions. Keep the model's
representational choices, the constraints supplied by observations and losses,
and the resulting scientific claims distinct.

## Core concepts and ownership

Keep these concepts related but distinct:

1. **Learning question and objective:** what is to be learned, what observations
   and conditioning are available, and which claims the loss and experiment
   can constrain.
2. **Representations and composition:** how observations, learned features,
   optional persistent state, and neural components fit together.
3. **Identity and structure:** which modeled entities and relations exist, with
   stable domain and order identity.
4. **Activity and eligibility:** which entities or relations participate in a
   particular evaluation; dense participation remains a valid choice.
5. **Values and parameters:** learned parameters, activations, optional persistent
   state, and their distinct ownership and generations.
6. **Logical and physical layout:** how logical identities map to storage and
   execution representations, including the inverse mapping needed for values
   and gradients.
7. **Prepared execution and runtime state:** reusable operation preparation,
   allocations, streams, device bindings, and actual execution lifetime.

A value update should not imply a structure rebuild unless the operation
contract requires it. Discovering eligible work is not the same as choosing a
physical layout, and neither alone proves adaptive execution. Keep biological
identity separate from an ordering selected for physical efficiency. Record
conversion, allocation, reuse, invalidation, stream, and complete-cost
boundaries per operation.

| Concern | Owner | Cellerator boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Tensors, standard layers, autograd, optimizers | PyTorch and other numerical/ML backends | Reuse established infrastructure where useful; keep Cellerator's native operations and backend choices first-class. |
| Biological representations, neural compositions, reusable objectives and training mechanisms | Cellerator | Make biological learning natural without requiring cell instances, transition rules, or a particular network family. |
| Model configuration, serialization, pretrained loading, and sharing interfaces | Cellerator | Preserve the model's biological input/output meaning and dependencies; integrate with existing artifact services. |
| Reusable cellular relations, support, dynamics, and operations | Cellerator | Define composable contracts and native entry points, with dynamics as one capability. |
| Scientific interpretation and model assumptions | Karyoplast, Cytoplast, Blastback, other consumers | Consumers choose biological meaning and validate their models. |
| Formal inferability of mechanisms or features | GlassHelix | Investigate question-specific identifiability and assumptions; Cellerator supplies reusable modeling and learning machinery. |
| Sequence-grounded representations | Baseplane | Cellerator consumes sequence-specific results without taking ownership of sequence semantics. |
| Persistence, sharding, transport, delivery | CellShard and owning systems | Integrate across explicit data boundaries. |
| Classical single-cell analysis | AnnData ecosystem, Scanpy, RAPIDS-singlecell | Remains upstream; `cellerator.adapters.anndata` offers explicit identity-aligned exchange without preprocessing or layer guessing. |

## Model reuse and sharing support {#building-training-and-sharing-cell-models}

**Supporting product framing recorded 2026-10-31.** A coherent model library and
ecosystem should make the biological ML abstractions above usable and reusable.
The Transformers analogy concerns this experience; it is subordinate to the
governing biological ML ambition. Researchers should be able to construct and
train cell models, load and adapt pretrained models, attach additional learned readouts, and share usable
model packages. This is an architectural direction; it does not assert that
these interfaces are already implemented or settle their method names.

Keep this experience minimal across different model families. A Geneformer-like
encoder can operate on expression observations, Karyoplast can condition on a
cell's event history, and Cytoplast can coordinate many private contexts using
shared learned modules. Common construction, training, and sharing conventions
should preserve those differences. They must not require tokenization, a
transformer, a clock, a state-transition rule, or one canonical latent vector.

A reusable model package should preserve enough information to instantiate and
interpret the model, with explicit references to any external dependencies:

| Concern | Information to preserve where applicable |
|---|---|
| Learned computation | Architecture configuration, shared parameters, and required component implementations. |
| Biological inputs | Feature identities, ordering, species or reference vocabulary, modality and representation conventions, and required preprocessing or conditioning. |
| Available outputs | Supported predictions and views, attached readout parameters, and the source representations and base-model revisions those readouts depend on. |
| Learning meaning | Documented objectives, supervision and conditioning, intended questions, assumptions, and bounded evaluation evidence. |
| Reuse and compatibility | Versioned loading contracts, component dependencies, and execution requirements needed to reproduce the declared computation. |

These are information responsibilities, not a fixed file format, mandatory
class hierarchy, or promise that every model answers every biological question.
For example, sharing an auxiliary ATAC readout should preserve its relationship
to the base model and source representation; loading it does not turn a
prediction into a measured ATAC profile.

Keep shared model artifacts distinct from individual cellular histories,
private recurrent memory, and training or population checkpoints. Those may
have their own save/resume contracts without becoming prerequisites for loading
every model. Device placement, expert residency, batching, and specialized
layouts remain execution concerns. Portable model meaning must not depend on
one transient placement, and portability must not force dense materialization
or replace native C++/CUDA execution with a mandatory Torch implementation.

Cellerator should own the model serialization, loading, and sharing interfaces
while reusing established artifact hosting and delivery. A possible
[Hugging Face Hub integration](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/models-adding-libraries)
would be one supporting interoperability route, and library registration could
be a later milestone. Neither defines Cellerator's distinctive purpose or
implies scientific endorsement, package maturity, or measured speedup. This framing authorizes no integration, registration, publication, or
code change by itself.

## Proposed package shape

This layout shows durable ownership destinations. The current-source route map
is maintained separately in [developer routing](development/routing.md); it
records current paths, owner, consumers, evidence, disposition, and maturity.
Until a unit has moved with its build targets, consumers, tests, and evidence,
its current path remains authoritative.

Package placement does not define a mandatory modeling pipeline. In particular,
existing state-transition packages and the current small `nn` surface do not
make dynamics the framework core or impose a ceiling on learned architectures.
This clarification changes architectural intent, not implementation paths.

```text
include/Cellerator/                 # public native contracts
  structure/ support/ indexing/     # identity and reusable work preparation
  layout/                           # logical-to-physical mapping contracts
  ops/<family>/                     # open-ended native operation families
src/                                 # native implementations, grouped by owner
  common/ structure/ support/ indexing/ gating/ layout/
  ops/<family>/                     # numeric, matrix, process, sparse, etc.
bindings/                            # thin Python and optional Torch adapters
python/cellerator/                   # installed Python package
  nn/ ops/ adapters/ torch/           # neural compositions, operations, integrations
  interactions/ inference/            # relationships and inference mechanisms
  modeling/ state/ events/ dynamics/  # optional model state, histories and evolution
  execution/ experimental/            # execution services and research candidates
bench/ experiments/                  # candidates and bounded evidence
```

Current code has begun to align with this structure. Native implementation
families include `src/common`, `src/structure`, `src/support`, `src/indexing`,
`src/gating`, `src/layout`, and several `src/ops` families. Their public
headers do not all mirror those directory names: identity is under
`include/Cellerator/structure`, while support, indexing, gating, and current
projection contracts remain under `include/Cellerator/compute`; operation
families are under `include/Cellerator/ops`. Python has `ops.py`, `nn.py`,
`torch/`, and `experimental/`. Existing compiler, runtime, tokenization, model,
and compatibility paths remain where their consumers and build contracts
place them. The routing document is the exhaustive path-level source of truth;
this architecture page avoids duplicating its changing inventory.

### Operation families

Group reusable computation by mathematical and model contract rather than by
one downstream application. A family should specify its inputs, outputs,
derivatives, precision, preparation/reuse behavior, supported backend, and
required identity/layout mappings. Keep the family space open. Do not add
placeholder modules for imagined future operations.

The `nn` namespace and other model-facing APIs should grow from reusable
representation, architecture, and learning needs. Their current small size is
an implementation fact. Reuse normal layers, autograd, and optimizers where
they already serve the computation; add biological compositions, objectives,
or native implementations where they improve modeling or execution. Avoid
duplicating established infrastructure without a concrete purpose. A useful
learned component need not be a new kernel or a state-transition wrapper.

### Sparse indexing, routing, and gating

Sparse indexing, support, routing, and gating are optional computational
opportunities. They help identify and execute eligible work when the model's
structure justifies it; they must not constrain which relationships a model may
learn or require a dense architecture to adopt sparse machinery. Dense attention
and dense learned transformations remain first-class. Keep general paths usable
without unnecessary routing or conversion overhead. Identity-preserving
structure, support selection, mapping work to mechanisms, and conditional execution each
need explicit contracts and invalidation rules. The existence of one fast
candidate does not establish a universal dispatcher or prove complete-model
speedup. Preserve dense, sparse, and alternate candidates when evidence does
not select one globally.

### Layout and execution semantics

Layout describes how logical model values are represented physically. It
must retain mappings that allow values, outputs, and derivatives to return to
their logical identities. Execution semantics state what is prepared, what is
reused, what values or structure invalidate it, and who owns device resources.
Separate discovery from physical realization and actual runtime state. Include
conversion, setup, allocation, and synchronization in a performance comparison
when those costs are part of the workload.

Execution fields are an experimental composition layer, not a prerequisite for
using operations. The current field composes a narrow prepared Product2 Torch
module on CPU and exposes explicit structure rebinding. It has no JIT or live
recompilation. Broader compiler and IR work remains available for research but
does not define the stable package surface.

### Experimental and upstream boundaries

The compiler, adaptive fields, tokenization, and candidate layout work remain
separately labeled by their actual maturity. An experimental implementation
can still be useful and routed; its location does not promote it to a stable
API. Classical single-cell analysis in the repository is a testbed or consumer,
not a replacement for Scanpy or RAPIDS-singlecell. AnnData is required by the
Python package, while numerical entry points currently accept explicit arrays
or tensors.

## Numerical policy

FP16 is Cellerator's general computation default when an operation's contract
supports it. It is a first-class arithmetic type for both SIMT and Tensor Core
implementations; Tensor Core use is an implementation choice, not a condition
for using FP16. FP32 and FP64 remain available as explicit alternatives, along
with other types already supported by a particular operation. FP32
accumulation is appropriate when it improves the operation's error behavior,
but each operation declares its own policy for storage, multiplication,
accumulation, and output.

This is the design policy; it does not claim that every current algorithm or
build configuration implements FP16 arithmetic. The source CMake defaults
currently select FP16 storage, FP32 computation, and FP32 accumulation for new,
unspecified real work. Author-reported tests on biological data support FP16
as a reasonable approximation so far, but exhaustive scientific validation
and a general error bound have not been established. Preserve per-operation
evidence and compare against the upstream/native computation or a suitable
higher-precision reference. See [Performance and Validation](performance_validation.qmd)
for the evidence and reporting contract.

Use templates when an algorithm is independent of numeric type; this keeps
one implementation and one semantic contract across types. Add type-specific
specialization only where arithmetic semantics, supported instructions, or
measured performance require it, and keep the declared precision contract
explicit.

## Migration rule

Move complete implementation units, not directory names. Before changing a
route, identify its callers, build targets, installed API, tests, evidence
records, and archived history. Keep unique native entry points and compatibility
consumers until each is deliberately redirected. The [routing document](development/routing.md)
shows current versus target placement; it is an inventory, not a mutable task
status report. Cleanup is complete only when every current artifact has an
explicit disposition and every gap is visible.
